content: 1. Alteplase is administered via transcatheter intra-arterial infusion at a dose of 1 mg/kg/hr for a duration of 1 to 8 hours or until thrombus lysis is achieved. 2. Alteplase is used in the treatment of intraventricular hemorrhage associated with intracerebral hemorrhage. 3. Alteplase has been granted orphan designation for the treatment of plastic bronchitis. 4. Defibrotide enhances the effects of alteplase through pharmacodynamic synergism. Co-administration of defibrotide with antithrombotic or fibrinolytic drugs is contraindicated. 5. Alteplase is not indicated for routine maintenance or reopening of central venous lines. 6. Co-administration of alteplase with apixaban increases anticoagulation effects. This combination should be avoided or alternative drugs should be considered. 7. Caplacizumab and alteplase both enhance each other’s anticoagulant effects. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 8. Zanubrutinib reduces the toxicity of alteplase through anticoagulation. However, zanubrutinib-induced cytopenias increase the risk of hemorrhage, especially when combined with antiplatelets or anticoagulants. 9. Alteplase and alfalfa both increase anticoagulation. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 10. American ginseng and alteplase both enhance anticoagulation. Therapy should be adjusted, and close monitoring is advised. 11. Antithrombin alfa and alteplase both increase anticoagulation. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 12. Antithrombin III and alteplase both enhance anticoagulation. Therapy should be adjusted, and close monitoring is required. 13. Argatroban and alteplase both increase anticoagulation. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 14. Aspirin and alteplase increase each other’s toxicity through anticoagulation. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is required. 15. The concurrent use of low-dose aspirin with anticoagulants or antiplatelet agents is common in patients with cardiovascular disease. Close monitoring is essential. 16. Aspirin rectal and alteplase both enhance anticoagulation. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 17. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and alteplase increase each other’s toxicity through anticoagulation. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. 18. Azficel-T and alteplase may increase bruising or bleeding at biopsy or injection sites when co-administered with anticoagulants or antiplatelets. Concomitant use is not recommended. Decisions regarding anticoagulant or antiplatelet therapy should be made by a physician. 19. Bivalirudin and alteplase both enhance anticoagulation. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 20. Celecoxib and alteplase both increase anticoagulation. Caution is advised due to the potential for increased bleeding risk. 21. Choline magnesium trisalicylate and alteplase both enhance anticoagulation. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 22. Cinnamon and alteplase both increase anticoagulation. Caution is advised as cinnamon may theoretically interact with blood-thinning medications due to its coumarin content. 23. Cordyceps and alteplase both enhance anticoagulation. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 24. Dabigatran and alteplase both increase anticoagulation and have the potential to cause bleeding. Concomitant use may increase bleeding risk. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 25. Dalteparin and alteplase both enhance anticoagulation. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 26. Danshen and alteplase both increase anticoagulation. Therapy should be adjusted, and close monitoring is necessary. 27. Devil’s claw and alteplase both enhance anticoagulation. Caution is advised as devil’s claw may have additive anticoagulant activity. 28. Diclofenac and alteplase both increase anticoagulation. Caution is advised due to the potential for increased bleeding risk. 29. Diflunisal and alteplase both enhance anticoagulation. Caution is advised due to the potential for increased bleeding risk. 30. Dong quai and alteplase both increase anticoagulation. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 31. Enoxaparin and alteplase both enhance anticoagulation. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 32. Epoprostenol and alteplase both increase anticoagulation. Caution is advised as co-administration may increase bleeding risk, although this was not observed in clinical trials. 33. Etodolac and alteplase both enhance anticoagulation. Caution is advised due to the potential for increased bleeding risk. 34. Fenoprofen and alteplase both increase anticoagulation. Caution is advised due to the potential for increased bleeding risk. 35. Feverfew and alteplase both enhance anticoagulation. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 36. Fish oil and alteplase may increase bleeding risk when taken together. Patients should be monitored periodically for prolonged bleeding. 37. Flurbiprofen and alteplase both enhance anticoagulation. Caution is advised due to the potential for increased bleeding risk. 38. Fondaparinux and alteplase both increase anticoagulation. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 39. Forskolin and alteplase both enhance anticoagulation. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary as forskolin may cause bleeding due to additive platelet inhibition. 40. Garlic and alteplase both increase anticoagulation. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 41. Ginger and alteplase both enhance anticoagulation. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. 42. Ginkgo biloba and alteplase both increase anticoagulation. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 43. Green tea and alteplase may increase bleeding risk when used together. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. 44. Heparin and alteplase both enhance anticoagulation. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 45. Horse chestnut seed and alteplase both increase anticoagulation. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 46. Ibrutinib increases the effects of alteplase through anticoagulation. Caution is advised as ibrutinib may increase the risk of hemorrhage in patients receiving antiplatelet or anticoagulant therapies. 47. Ibuprofen and alteplase both enhance anticoagulation. Caution is advised due to the potential for increased bleeding risk. 48. Imatinib and alteplase may increase each other’s toxicity. Imatinib may cause thrombocytopenia, increasing bleeding risk when co-administered with anticoagulants, NSAIDs, platelet inhibitors, or thrombolytic agents. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 49. Indomethacin and alteplase both enhance anticoagulation. Caution is advised due to the potential for increased bleeding risk. 50. Ketoprofen and alteplase both increase anticoagulation. Caution is advised due to the potential for increased bleeding risk. 51. Ketorolac and alteplase both enhance anticoagulation. Caution is advised due to the potential for increased bleeding risk. 52. Melatonin increases the effects of alteplase through anticoagulation. Caution is advised as melatonin may decrease prothrombin time. 53. Meloxicam and alteplase both enhance anticoagulation. Caution is advised due to the potential for increased bleeding risk. 54. Nabumetone and alteplase both increase anticoagulation. Caution is advised due to the potential for increased bleeding risk. 55. Naproxen and alteplase both enhance anticoagulation. Caution is advised due to the potential for increased bleeding risk. 56. Nitroglycerin rectal reduces the effects of alteplase. Caution is advised as nitroglycerin decreases the thrombolytic effect of tissue-type plasminogen activator (t-PA). Plasma levels of t-PA are reduced when co-administered with nitroglycerin. 57. Omega-3 fatty acids and alteplase may increase bleeding risk. Patients should be monitored periodically for prolonged bleeding. 58. Oxaprozin and alteplase both enhance anticoagulation. Caution is advised due to the potential for increased bleeding risk. 59. Panax ginseng and alteplase both increase anticoagulation. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 60. Piroxicam and alteplase both enhance anticoagulation. Caution is advised due to the potential for increased bleeding risk. 61. Reishi and alteplase both increase anticoagulation. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 62. Rivaroxaban and alteplase both enhance anticoagulation. Avoid concurrent use due to increased bleeding risk, except during therapeutic transition periods. Monitor for signs of blood loss. 63. Salsalate and alteplase both enhance anticoagulation. Caution is advised due to the potential for increased bleeding risk. 64. Siberian ginseng and alteplase both increase anticoagulation. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 65. Sulindac and alteplase both enhance anticoagulation. Caution is advised due to the potential for increased bleeding risk. 66. Tenecteplase and alteplase both increase anticoagulation. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 67. Ticagrelor and alteplase both enhance anticoagulation. Caution is advised due to the increased risk of bleeding during concomitant use. 68. Tranexamic acid and alteplase exhibit pharmacodynamic antagonism, reducing each other’s effects. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 69. Vorapaxar and alteplase both enhance anticoagulation. Caution is advised, and periodic monitoring is necessary due to the increased risk of bleeding. 70. Vortioxetine and alteplase both increase anticoagulation. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is required. 71. Ceftaroline increases the effects of alteplase. Cephalosporins with a methylthiotetrazole (MTT) side ring are associated with hypoprothrombinemic activity. Close monitoring is advised.
